sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Precision CO2 Laser Cutting of 3D Mechanical Wooden Puzzles

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (TW; sub-national jurisdiction operating its own company registry and investment-administered regime under the composite key)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system; German-Japanese codified tradition; judicial interpretations of the Supreme Court as persuasive-biding precedents)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), signed 29 June 2010 — early-harvest services and trade concessions
Cross-Strait Agreement on the Protection of Investors and Promotion of Investment, in force 1 February 2013 — substantive investment protection for PRC investors in Taiwan
Cross-Strait Agreement on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Tax Cooperation, signed 25 December 2015 — signed but not yet entered into force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Company Act (公司法), Article 22-1, as inserted by the 2018 Company Act Amendment (effective 1 November 2018) — annual electronic declaration of substantial controllers/UBOs to the Ministry of Economic Affairs; Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法), consolidated by the 2019 amendment — customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership identification obligations; Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (資恐防制法), 2016 — sanctions screening and asset freezing; Rules Governing Investment by Mainland Chinese Persons (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法) and the Examination Guidelines of the Investment Commission, MOEA — mandatory piercing of PRC investors to ultimate natural-person shareholders and state-affiliation review for all investments equal to or above 25%; additionally, the MOEA Company Registration Fee Standards and Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Examination Regulations govern the registry mechanics.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and current Business License (營業執照) of the PRC parent/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-strait Consular Legalization Equivalent: PRC notarization by a competent PRC notary office followed by ARATS authentication and Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification; Hague Apostille not applicable because Taiwan is not a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited financial statements of the PRC investor for the most recent complete fiscal year
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC-registered Certified Public Accounting firm (with the investor's audit report)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization → ARATS authentication → SEF verification (Consular Legalization); no apostille route available

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate evidencing source of funds and lawful foreign-exchange remittance (資金來源及結匯證明)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC remitting bank (with SAFE cross-border payment record) and the Taiwan receiving bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization of the bank certificate followed by cross-strait double verification; the Taiwan bank's inward-remittance certificate requires no apostille but must be original

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police Clearance Certificate / Certificate of No Criminal Record for every director, alternate director, and natural-person UBO proposed for the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau (PSB), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization and cross-strait verification through SEF/ARATS; individual fingerprints or biometric notarization may be required by the issuing bureau

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Taiwan law firm and local designated representative for the incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC investor company (signed by legal representative and notarized in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by cross-strait notarization and SEF verification; original notarized copy required by the Investment Commission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Investment Application File and business plan (投資申請書暨營運計畫書) submitted to the Investment Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant WFOE via the Taiwan designated attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local statutory filing — no apostille/consular step; notarization of the responsible person's signature before a Taiwan notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory cumulative screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, supervisors, general manager, finance officer, and authorized signatories at onboarding and continuously thereafter against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the Taiwan Ministry of Justice counter-terrorism designation list issued under Article 3 of the Counter-Terrorism Financing Act; (v) Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission prohibited-investor and AML blacklists; and (vi) global PEP databases covering Taiwan government officials and foreign PEPs per FATF recommendations 12 and 24. Because the investor chain originates in mainland China, enhanced due diligence is mandatory under the Investment Commission's National Security Review, including inquiry into ultimate PRC state-affiliation, military-industrial ties, and export-control exposure of the CO2 laser equipment under US EAR/ECCN controls. Negative-news media screening and beneficial-ownership tracing through any nominee/intermediate holding layers (including Hong Kong and British Virgin Islands vehicles) must be performed prior to filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Company and Commerce One-Stop Registration Platform (公司及商業一站式線上申請) — https://onestop.nat.gov.tw; public name-availability search: Company Registration Public Information Inquiry (商工登記公示資料查詢服務) — https://findbiz.nat.gov.tw; name pre-check application administered by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Commercial Administration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 18 of the Company Act, the registered corporate name must be in Traditional Chinese characters; the name must contain a distinct distinguishing feature and a designated business type title ('有限公司'). A romanized English name may be additionally recorded at registration, but it cannot be the sole registered name; transliteration to/from Chinese should follow the Hanyu Pinyin standard adopted by the Ministry of the Interior, and the English name must not be identical to an existing registered English company name in Taiwan. Documents executed by the WFOE should dual-stamp with the Chinese name and the English counterpart for banking and payment-rail onboarding.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms requiring prior ministerial approval: 銀行 (bank), 保險 (insurance), 信託 (trust), 證券 (securities), 期貨 (futures), 金融 (financial) — require Financial Supervisory Commission authorization
Terms implying public or state character: 政府 (government), 國家 (national), 中央 (central), 北市 (city), 合作社 (cooperative) — require consent of the relevant competent authority or are strictly restricted

Licensed professional terms: 律師 (lawyer), 會計師 (CPA), 建築師 (architect), 醫師 (medical practitioner), 記帳士 (bookkeeper) — require the underlying professional license and are prohibited in the corporate name absent licensure

Cross-strait sensitive tokens: 中國 (China), 大陸 (Mainland), 兩岸 (cross-strait), 中華 (Chinese) in company names trigger mandatory Investment Commission and MOEA expedited review and are generally disfavored for private WFOEs
Misleading or public-order-violating tokens: any name suggesting illegal activities, monopolies, or royalties such as 獨占, 國營, 警政, 郵政 without authorization

Identical or confusingly similar names: any name identical to an existing registered company, or so similar as to cause third-party confusion (including identical Chinese romanization/English names), which is a statutory refusal ground
Generic-only names lacking a distinguishing feature: names composed solely of common trading descriptions (e.g., 木製拼圖) without a distinctive identifier are rejected
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under the Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Examination Regulations: (1) within 15 days from receipt of the rejection notice, the applicant may file a reconsideration (申請複查) with the MOEA Commercial Administration, attaching amended name candidates and supporting arguments; (2) if reconsideration fails, an administrative appeal (訴願) must be lodged with the MOEA Appeals Committee within 30 days of the reconsideration service; (3) the final recourse is an administrative action before the Taipei High Administrative Court, to be filed within 2 months of the appeal decision. The 6-month name reservation cannot be extended; if registration is not completed before expiry, a fresh name pre-check application must be filed. In similarity-based rejections, the applicant may also submit a notarized written consent from the prior registered name holder to overcome the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole registered office. Taiwan's Company Act and the Factory Registration Act require the WFOE to maintain a physical operational presence. Because the scope is precision CO2 laser cutting and mechanical wooden puzzle assembly (ISIC 3240), the registered office must be a real leased or owned industrial/commercial address under the company's tenant rights; an administrative correspondence address may differ, but the factory site itself must be registered with the municipal competent authority under factory registration requirements. A mailbox-only virtual service address will be rejected by the registrar and by the Investment Commission during capital verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified: approximately 40% probability of an unannounced occupational-safety/fire-prevention inspection within the first 12 months of operations (laser equipment and combustible wood dust are key triggers); approximately 90% probability of a scheduled factory-registration on-site inspection before commencement of laser operations; less than 5% probability of an AML/CFT supervisory inspection given the Low_Risk_Standard tier and the absence of statutory licensing requirements; periodic toy-safety (CNS) market-surveillance sampling by BSMI is foreseeable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, principally Articles 1, 17, 128-156, 387-393 and 398-403; Foreign Investment Act, principally Articles 4, 7-8 and 20; Business Registration Act, principally Articles 4-8 and 15-18. A foreign-owned Taiwan subsidiary is generally incorporated as a Taiwan company limited by shares or company limited by capital contribution, rather than as a mainland-China WFOE.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent municipal or county government business registration authority under delegated jurisdiction; foreign investment approval is handled by the Investment Review Division of the Department of Investment Promotion, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請書), supported by the approved company name and business scope reservation, foreign investment approval application where applicable, articles of incorporation, shareholder or incorporator documents, director and supervisor consents, capital verification evidence, and registered-office documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum paid-in capital for an ordinary company limited by shares. Capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and establishment costs. No general statutory escrow account is required, but the subscribed capital must be remitted to the company-designated Taiwan bank account and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant before or during registration. Foreign investors must obtain foreign investment approval before capital remittance where the investment falls within the Foreign Investment Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscription by [Shareholder] for [number] ordinary shares at NT$[amount] per share and authorize issuance upon receipt and verification of the subscribed capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at [full Taiwan address] be adopted as the Company’s principal office and service address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name] be appointed Chairperson, [name] be appointed General Manager, and [name] be appointed Company Secretary or responsible corporate officer, each effective immediately, subject to applicable registration. Any director is authorized to execute filings, banking documents, investment applications, and ancillary instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce online company name and business scope pre-check system, or the competent local registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese and English names, principal business activities, proposed company form, and registered jurisdiction. Use Taiwan business codes corresponding to toy manufacturing, wooden products, laser processing, assembly, wholesale, and export activities. Confirm that the scope does not include restricted or specially licensed activities. Obtain the name and business scope pre-check approval before preparing final incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Proposed English company name, if used
Business scope statement and Taiwan business classification codes
Power of attorney for local agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the name or business codes and resubmit. If the authority identifies a restricted activity, remove it or obtain the relevant sector approval before filing the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Division, Department of Investment Promotion, Ministry of Economic Affairs, through the online foreign investment application system or designated filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign investor identity, ownership chain, investment amount, source of funds, proposed Taiwan company structure, business plan, and investment purpose. Foreign corporate documents must be notarized or otherwise authenticated in the country of issuance and translated into Chinese where required. Do not remit subscribed capital until the investment approval and banking instructions are confirmed.
required_dossiers: Investor certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer written queries within the stated deadline, provide missing ownership or source-of-funds evidence, revise the business plan, or withdraw and refile after correcting restricted-activity or documentation issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company incorporator, proposed directors and supervisors, and Taiwan notary or certifying professional where notarization is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation, subscription or incorporation record, director and supervisor appointment documents, office consent, and corporate authorization instruments. For a company limited by shares, appoint the statutory board and supervisor structure required by the selected company form. Execute foreign corporate documents with applicable notarization, apostille, legalization, or Taiwan-recognized authentication and provide certified Chinese translations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct execution defects, obtain missing signatures or authentication, replace disqualified officers, and re-execute inconsistent articles or resolutions before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Account and Complete Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank designated by the incorporator; Taiwan certified public accountant for capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a preparatory account in the company name or designated incorporation format, remit the approved foreign investment amount, retain bank remittance and balance evidence, and instruct a Taiwan certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report. Do not use capital for operating expenditure before registration unless legally and operationally permitted by the bank and applicable rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reconcile remittance discrepancies, correct investor-name or currency mismatches, obtain a replacement bank certificate, and submit a supplemental CPA report if the registrar questions the capital evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent municipal or county government online company registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Registration Application with approved name, articles, shareholder and officer information, registered-office proof, investment approval, CPA capital verification, and required declarations. Pay the prescribed filing fee. After approval, obtain the company registration certificate and complete business registration, tax registration, company seal registration, and beneficial-owner or responsible-person filings required by the competent authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar's deficiency notice, correct forms or business codes, replace defective evidence, and resubmit within the prescribed cure period. A refusal may generally be challenged through administrative appeal or a new corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Tax, Customs, Banking, and Employment Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau branch; Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; Labor Insurance Bureau; National Health Insurance Administration; and the company’s designated bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company tax account and invoice status, establish customs importer-exporter capability if goods will cross borders, activate corporate banking, and enroll employees in mandatory labor insurance, employment insurance, occupational accident insurance, and national health insurance as applicable. Establish accounting books, invoice controls, payroll records, and transfer-pricing documentation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or customs registration data, submit missing employment records, and request written clarification from the relevant branch before commencing taxable sales or imports.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Factory, Fire, Workplace, and Environmental Approvals Before Production
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local government economic development or industrial development department, local fire department, local building authority, occupational safety authority, and relevant environmental authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before installing or operating production machinery, confirm whether the premises meet the Factory Management Act factory-registration thresholds. Submit factory-location, building, equipment, process, fire, environmental, and occupational-safety documents as applicable. Do not commence laser cutting or commercial production until required approvals, inspections, and utility or emissions permissions are complete.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure inspection findings, submit revised layouts or equipment controls, obtain additional permits, and request reinspection. Suspend affected operations until the authority confirms compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Competent local government economic development or industrial development department under the Factory Management Act, with the Ministry of Economic Affairs serving as the central industrial-policy authority. Factory registration is conditional on premises, equipment, workforce, power, and production thresholds and is separate from company registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration (工廠登記), where the operation meets statutory factory-registration thresholds; otherwise, business registration and any applicable environmental, fire, building, machinery, and occupational-safety approvals are required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, including the competent local environmental protection bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally EIA exempt for a small wooden-puzzle laser assembly facility unless the site, industrial-zone development, scale, land-use change, or listed project category triggers the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. Separate environmental permits may still be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Operate only within approved air-emission, wastewater, noise, and waste-management limits. Laser cutting of wood may generate particulate matter, smoke, VOCs, and odors; install suitable local exhaust, filtration, and fire controls. Obtain an air-pollution control permit if regulated emission thresholds are met. Discharge wastewater only under applicable Water Pollution Control Act standards and permits. Classify and transfer hazardous or regulated waste through licensed contractors; maintain manifests and records. Do not discharge untreated process wastewater, burn wood waste on site, or vent emissions without required controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain building-use and occupancy confirmation, fire safety equipment approval and periodic inspection from the local fire department, and structural or load verification for machinery and storage areas where required. Implement occupational safety controls under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including laser guarding, interlocks, ventilation, emergency stops, electrical safety, combustible-dust and fire-risk controls, personal protective equipment, training, chemical and waste inventories, and accident reporting. Obtain hazardous-work, pressure-equipment, lifting-equipment, or other specialized inspections if the installed equipment triggers those requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Assumption: Taiwan is the operative jurisdiction because jurisdiction_id is TW. The competent authorities are the Ministry of Finance of Taiwan (MOF), the relevant National Taxation Bureau, and the MOF eTax Portal. Company registration is administered separately by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. A mainland-China WFOE cannot use a Taiwan tax identity without a separately registered Taiwan company, branch, or other legally recognized establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine whether the business will operate through a Taiwan subsidiary, Taiwan branch, or other taxable fixed establishment. 2. Obtain foreign-investment approval or establish the Taiwan entity through the Ministry of Economic Affairs, where applicable. 3. File company or branch registration, business scope, responsible-person information, registered address, capital and organizational documents. 4. Submit tax registration to the competent National Taxation Bureau using the company registration certificate, articles or branch documents, responsible-person identification, lease or premises evidence, bank information, and foreign-investor corporate documents. 5. Provide certified Chinese translations and authentication or verification documents for foreign corporate records when required. 6. Obtain the Taiwan Unified Business Number (統一編號), which functions as the principal business tax and income-tax identifier. 7. Register for business tax and select the applicable VAT filing status. 8. Register for electronic invoicing and obtain an approved certificate, provider connection, or MOF platform access. 9. Register customs and trade credentials with the relevant customs systems if importing or exporting goods. 10. Maintain separate registrations for any branches, factories, warehouses, or fixed establishments that independently trigger tax obligations. The Taiwan tax identifier is not the same as a mainland-China Taxpayer Identification Number or a mainland Unified Social Credit Code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan has no general United States-style check-the-box election and no broad elective hybrid-mismatch classification regime. A Taiwan limited company is generally subject to Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax on its Taiwan taxable income, while a Taiwan branch of a foreign company is taxed under branch rules. Business tax treatment is determined by statutory classification, including ordinary VAT treatment, small-business assessment treatment where legally available, and zero-rating for qualifying transactions; these are registrations or statutory treatments rather than freely elective entity classifications. Taiwan controlled-foreign-company and transfer-pricing rules may apply to qualifying Taiwan tax residents and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For small-business assessment purposes, the commonly applicable monthly sales thresholds are approximately NT$80,000 for goods businesses and NT$40,000 for service businesses. These thresholds do not provide a general exemption from registration where a business is carrying on taxable commercial activity, imports goods, operates through a taxable establishment, or is otherwise required to register. Ordinary VAT taxpayers generally register before commencing business and file bi-monthly business-tax returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses a government-supervised electronic invoice system rather than a universal Latin-American-style real-time pre-clearance model. Businesses required to issue electronic invoices must use the MOF e-Invoice Platform or an approved service provider, maintain approved electronic certificate credentials, generate compliant invoice numbers and formats, transmit invoice and deduction information through the prescribed system or API, and retain electronic records. Electronic invoices must contain statutory seller, buyer, transaction, tax, amount, date, and identification information. Certain B2B and B2C categories are subject to electronic-invoicing requirements and implementation schedules. Customs export declarations are processed through customs systems separately from VAT invoicing. Failure to issue, transmit, preserve, or correct electronic invoices can lead to tax assessments and administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exports of goods may be zero-rated where the goods are exported from Taiwan under customs control and the export is supported by the customs declaration and related commercial records. The export transaction must be attributable to the Taiwan VAT registrant and must not be a domestic sale disguised as an export. Services may qualify for zero-rating where they are supplied to a foreign customer, used outside Taiwan, and satisfy the applicable statutory conditions; services performed or consumed in Taiwan generally do not qualify merely because the customer is foreign. The taxpayer must report the zero-rated sales in the VAT return and retain commercial contracts, purchase orders, invoices, shipping records, customs evidence, proof of foreign customer status, payment records, foreign-exchange settlement evidence, and evidence of offshore use for services. Input VAT refunds require valid input invoices or customs duty documents, proper accounting records, and reconciliation of the claimed input tax with the zero-rated export turnover.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs Export Declaration or equivalent electronic customs record showing the Taiwan exporter, goods, value, destination, and export status
Sales contract, purchase order, or other transaction agreement
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport document
Proof of export completion, including customs release or shipment confirmation where required
Foreign-exchange settlement or inward-remittance evidence, bank collection record, or legally acceptable alternative payment evidence
Input VAT invoices and import VAT payment documents supporting any refund claim
For offshore services: service agreement, foreign customer identification, deliverables, evidence of offshore use, invoice, and payment trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The taxpayer must be able to reconcile the zero-rated invoice, VAT return, customs declaration, accounting ledger, shipping evidence, contract, and payment or foreign-exchange record. The National Taxation Bureau may deny zero-rating, reclassify the transaction as taxable domestic turnover, assess the unpaid 5% business tax, impose statutory interest, and recover or claw back improperly refunded input VAT. False export declarations, fabricated shipping documents, sham offshore-service claims, circular transactions, undisclosed domestic use, or fictitious payment evidence may trigger administrative penalties under the Business Tax Act and related tax laws; tax-evasion penalties can be calculated by reference to the tax evaded and may reach multiples of the evaded tax. Serious cases may also create criminal exposure under Taiwan tax, customs, document-fraud, or money-laundering laws. Export proceeds are generally subject to Taiwan foreign-exchange settlement and reporting requirements, with a commonly applicable six-month period equivalent to 180 days; extensions, alternative settlement methods, and sector-specific exceptions must be verified with the Central Bank and the taxpayer's authorized bank.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the monetary authority, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the specialized FX regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a partial convertibility regime. Current account transactions, including profit remittances, are handled under a verifiable authenticity framework; they can be converted through banks without pre-approval, provided the underlying transaction documents, audited retained earnings, tax clearance and economic substance evidence are supplied. The capital account remains highly controlled: foreign direct investment injection, shareholder loans, capital reduction and exit proceeds require SAFE registration through a designated bank and are generally convertible only after compliance verification and full tax clearance. Taiwan-sourced investment is treated as foreign investment under the mainland's negative-list regime and receives no special profit-repatriation quota beyond audited distributable reserves.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished mandatory surrender ratios. Exporters may freely retain export receipts in foreign currency or settle 100% into RMB. All export proceeds must be credited to a domestic trade foreign exchange account within the monitored trade receipt period, generally within 90 days from the date of export customs declaration. Advance receipts must be matched to actual export within 30 days or registered in the SAFE trade monitoring system. RMB settlement occurs at the bank's listed rate after verification of the customs declaration, commercial invoice, and transport documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account + Capital FX Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic RMB Deposit Account + Multi-Currency Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Moderate. Offshore electronic money institutions such as Airwallex, Wise and Payoneer cannot independently open local CNY accounts or provide SAFE-cleared settlement for a WFOE. They may be used as collection adjuncts for Amazon Pay and Stripe proceeds, but all final CNY conversion and treasury execution must be channelled through a licensed onshore bank or a licensed cross-border payment institution to avoid violating PBOC and SAFE regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All major Chinese banks require the legal representative or a lawfully authorised resident representative to attend a physical in-person interview during account opening. Fully remote opening for a foreign-invested WFOE is exceptional and subject to branch risk policies. Directors located in Taiwan may appoint a representative under a notarised and Chinese-consular certified power of attorney, but the appointed resident must still appear physically for biometric AML/KYC verification. Supplementary directors may sometimes complete video verification, but the primary signatory cannot.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owner with an opaque or layered ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents and share register; notarised and Chinese-consular certified board/owner resolutions; beneficial owner declaration signed by every direct or indirect shareholder holding over 25%; a full organisational chart tracing Taiwan treasury entities to ultimate human persons; audited financial statements of the immediate Taiwanese parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared ISIC activity, commercial invoice descriptions, and customs declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Precision CO2 laser cutting engineering drawings; product datasheet with 3D wooden puzzle bill of materials; supplier purchase contracts with Taiwanese timber/board vendors; freight forwarding agreements with Chinese logistics counterparties; export customs declarations and Form 10 records; certified Copy of Business License with the WFOE's actual business scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency small-value collections from Amazon Pay and Stripe aggregators not visibly matched by export declaration files
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly reconciliation report between aggregator payouts and the trade receivable ledger; per-order export summary; customs declarations and FX settlement records; logistics and last-mile tracking numbers; platform service agreements; treasury ledger demonstrating the use of proceeds in operating expenses and the repayment of any shareholder loans.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first obtain its business license and then open a basic RMB account and a foreign exchange settlement account at a licensed domestic bank. The bank files the Foreign Investment Information Report and completes the SAFE FDI Registration. The Taiwanese investor then sends a SWIFT MT103 remittance with purpose code 'FDI Capital Contribution' and the unique Foreign Investment Credential Number. The bank verifies the capital account and performs conversion into RMB through the Capital Settlement module, recording the receipt to qualified foreign capital status for subsequent profit remittance or equity transfer purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 instructions for telegraphic transfers, supported by commercial invoices, purchase orders, customs declarations and the trade foreign exchange monitoring code issued by the bank. For larger transactions or at the seller's request, the WFOE may issue a commercial letter of credit through SWIFT MT700, governed by UCP600; documents are presented and paid via MT756. Where the counterparty supports it, RMB cross-border trade settlement can use the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) alongside SWIFT to reduce correspondent fees and speed up availability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY FX forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank under the real-demand principle
FX swaps and currency swaps with licensed domestic banks for current account and capital account hedging
Cross-currency interest rate swaps with a licensed domestic bank upon SAFE registration and underlying loan documentation
NDF contracts are not permissible onshore for the WFOE; any such instrument should only be used by an offshore licensed vehicle dealing in CNH, not by the mainland entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Enterprise Income Tax rate for resident enterprises under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Art. 4, applicable to the China-resident WFOE.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for accredited High-New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); Small Low-Profit Enterprise effective rate of 5% on annual taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000 (2023-2027 policy: 25% of deemed taxable income at 20% rate); 100% additional deduction for qualified R&D expenses; 100% additional deduction for wages of disabled personnel; 10-year tax loss carryforward for HNTE and Sci-Tech SMEs under Announcement 2018 No. 45.
